# Three ways to misuse a sort key

Each mark below draws exactly one report, and each report is about the mark
rather than about any one back-end — so every one of them reaches an author
writing to a format that builds no index at all.

A sort key on a mark that indexes nothing has nothing to sort. The mark is
empty and carries no `entry=`, so there is no entry for the key to place:
[]{.index sort="Nowhere"}

A sort key deeper than the entry it sorts. The entry is the visible term,
which is always a single level, so the second sort level places nothing:
[Solo]{.index sort="first!second"}.

One entry given two different sort keys files in two places, which is not
something an index can do. The first mark in document order is the one that
wins, and the second is reported: [Ambivalence]{.index sort="Aaa"} and later
[Ambivalence]{.index sort="Bbb"}.
